messages:
ana: Heads-up — started seeing a p99 spike (~40ms) on paged-attn nodes after the last allocator tweak. Looks correlated with slab splits + KV page spills during medium batch bursts (seq ~512).

ana: Quick summary of what I saw from the flame: kernel choose falls back from fused-attn -> flashv1 when a slotspill path triggers, which increases per-token work and knocks the batching heuristic out of the sweet spot.

ana: Repro microtrace: a 64-request burst with variable seq lengths, ~30% long tokens. When the blocktable does a slab-split we get an extra copy and an eviction cascade: cpu + memcpy + kernel fallback.

ana: Paste of the allocation hot loop we instrumented (pseudocode):

```
alloc_page = find_hot_slot(anchor_key)
if alloc_page.free < needed && can_split(alloc_page):
  split_page(alloc_page)  # causes move and invalidates some KV refs
else:
  use_hot_prefix(alloc_page)
```

liam: I saw the same on benchbox earlier — split threshold is too aggressive for mixed workloads. We tuned it to 0.6 free -> 0.2 free recently, that reduces headroom. Lowering split threshold back to 0.45 reduced observed slotspills in perf bench.

liam: Two quick mitigation ideas: anchor hot prefixes (pin a small reserved region per slab) or do background split/compaction off the hot path. Anchoring example: reserve N small pages for hot prefixes so they don't force splits mid-request.

soo: Anchoring helps latency but increases steady-state memory. If we reserve too many pages we blow out dedicated pool cost. Also careful: pinning prevents compaction later -> fragmentation. :thinking_face:

marta: Can we instrument a per-prefix eviction counter? I want a small telemetry to show how many splits originate from which model+session. If it's a handful of hot prefixes, anchoring is cheap. If it's uniform, background compaction might be better.

ana: Good call. I saw ~12 prefixes account for 70% of splits during the window, so anchoring seems promising. Will add a counter.

liam: Another angle: kernel selection policy should prefer fused-attn for short-ish requests even if KV page missing, by forcing a KV-prefetch step that happens inline but without triggering full split. That avoids fallback to flashv1. In practice: add a two-step choose -> attempt-prefetch -> run-fused (if prefetch ok) flow.

marta: That risks adding latency for cases where prefetch fails. We should bound the prefetch time and fall back after X microseconds. Also add metrics for prefetch success rate by seq len.

soo: I worry about a prefetch that races with eviction. If prefetch grabs a page and the slab split moves the anchor, we can get stale refs. Need a generation check or index fingerprint.

ana: Agreed. We can use a simple per-page epoch that increments on split/compact; prefetch checks epoch before running fused kernel. If mismatch -> abort and fallback. Cheap and deterministic.

liam: Proposed config changes to test on canary:
- slab_split_threshold = 0.45
- anchor_reserved_pages = 4 per-slab
- prefetch_timeout_us = 1200
- prefetch_epoch_check = true

marta: I can run the fused vs flash microbench with those settings on canary if infra approves. Wanted seq lengths: 128/512/2048, batch sizes 8/32/64. We'll capture p50/p95/p99 and kernel switch counts.

infra-bot: Can deploy to paged-attn-canary in zone eu-west-1. Request ID: /deploy 1749994337 by ana. ETA ~15m.

deploy-bot: Started rollout to paged-attn-canary @ 1749994342. Will monitor kernel-choice, slab-splits, and p99 latency.

ana: Thanks — I'll push instrumentation change (per-prefix split counter + per-page epoch) and a short telemetry dashboard. Also will add unit for prefetch epoch check.

soo: If canary looks good let's try background compaction as a follow-up instead of reserving more pages long-term. Background compaction can run at low IO priority and shrink fragmentation.

marta: Actionable: I'll schedule microbench suite after deploy finishes and share results in this thread. If fused wins for 128/512 and no prefetch failures, we can keep prefetch enabled.

ana: Action items (from me): add metrics, small allocator patch (threshold -> 0.45), add epoch guard, enable anchor=4 on canary. I'll post a short diff here.

ana: Thanks all — will report back with numbers. :thumbsup:
